_comment: Copy to ~/.traicker/config.json. Every key is optional.
_idleTimeoutMinutes: A focus interval runs at most this long. Beyond it you were away, not orchestrating.
_idleAttributionCapMinutes: Ceiling on how much of ONE gap is reported as idle. An overnight gap is off the clock, not idle — without this the number is dominated by hours nobody was going to work.
_stitchGapMinutes: Gaps this short are absorbed into a billable block. The pause between an agent finishing and your next prompt is you reading the output, not a stop in the work.
_maxSpans: Ceilings for spans that never closed — a crash, a hard kill, a session still running.
_promptExcerptChars: Fallback label length when Claude Code has not generated a session title yet. Set to 0 to never store prompt text at all.
_translationModel: Model that writes and translates timesheet descriptions. An OpenRouter slug — provider-prefixed, and it must support structured outputs (openrouter.ai/models?supported_parameters=structured_outputs). Both jobs are light and the default is priced accordingly; 'anthropic/claude-opus-5' costs roughly 60x more per call, which is a decision about your money rather than one made for you. Credentials come from OPENROUTER_API_KEY.
_llmBaseUrl: OpenAI-compatible endpoint the model calls go to. A setting because the endpoint and the key travel together — pointing this elsewhere without also changing OPENROUTER_API_KEY sends your key to a host that did not issue it.
_modelPricing: Illustrative example only — check your provider's current published rates before trusting these numbers. Keyed by the exact model name Claude Code itself reports (visible on the dashboard's Models tab). Each model is a LIST of rates, one per effectiveFrom date: a day's usage is priced with the most recent entry at or before that day, so a rate change never rewrites the cost of a month already worked. A single entry with an old effectiveFrom is enough if the rate has never changed. Feeds an internal cost ESTIMATE only, never shown to a client. cacheWritePerMillion/cacheReadPerMillion are optional; omitted, those tokens count as $0 toward the estimate rather than guessing a rate.
_ignorePaths: Matches a path and everything under it. A DECLARED project always wins over an ignore prefix, and so does anything inside a declared WORKSPACE (a declared path that contains other declared paths) — ignoring the workspace directory is how you stop bare sessions started in it from becoming a project, without deleting the projects that live inside it. To drop a whole tree, ignore a path you have not declared.
_projects: A directory you work in becomes a project the first time an event arrives from it — nothing here is required. What this block adds is everything the filesystem cannot know: the client's name, and whether the time is billable.

C:/dev/acme-payments.name: Acme Payments
C:/dev/acme-payments._color: Hex colour used for this project everywhere it is drawn. Omit to derive one from the project id — that derived hue is a function of insertion order, so adding a project can recolour one you had already learned to recognise. Editable in the dashboard's Settings tab.
C:/dev/acme-payments._billable: Defaults to FALSE for any project not listed here. Most directories you open are your own; billing is the exception, and the two mistakes cost differently — an unmarked client is a project visibly missing from a total, while an unmarked personal project quietly inflates a figure the client reads.

commitment._kind: 'cap' is a ceiling, breached from above and flagged immediately. 'target' is a commitment, breached from below and only judged at week end. Opposite obligations — they deliberately do not share a field.

billing._note: Presence of this block is what makes a project appear in the dashboard's timesheet panel.
billing._basis: 'occupancy' bills the wall-clock the project was worked on, by you or by an agent you directed. 'focus' bills only your attention — far smaller, and right only if the client is buying presence rather than delivery.
billing._allowExcerpts: When Claude Code produced no title for a session, allow a raw slice of your prompt as the description. Off by default — an excerpt is unedited text you typed to an agent, often in the wrong language for the client.
billing._translateTo: Translate descriptions into this language before the client sees them. Cached per source string, so the same week always reads identically; fill the cache with `traicker translate --project X`. Omit to leave labels in the language the work happened in. Your own `traicker note` always wins over a translation.

C:/dev/northwind-crm.name: Northwind CRM
C:/dev/northwind-crm._note: A commitment without a billing block: weekly hours you track for yourself, with no timesheet to submit.
